nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of Kew Bulletin?
nodes.answer: The primary focus of Kew Bulletin is to publish high-quality research on plant and fungal taxonomy and systematics.
nodes.paragraph: :(123456789)Kew Bulletin DOi 10.1007/s12225-25-10253-4 the Board of trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, 2025A new Chapter for Kew Bulletin Manuel Luj n1 It has been a year since I assumed the role of Editor-in- Chief of Kew Bulletin , a journal with a legacy stretching back to 1887, when it was first published as Kew Gar - den S Bulletin of Miscellaneous Information. Following in the footsteps of my esteemed predecessor, Dr Tim Utteridge, who guided the Bulletin to new heights, is a significant responsibility. However, I am excited by the challenge and eager to build upon the journal S long and illustrious history. My vision for Kew Bulletin is to maintain and enhance its position as the premier platform for pub- lishing high-quality research on plant and fungal tax- onomy and systematics by the global botanical com- munity. We will uphold the rigorous standards that have established the Bulletin as a trusted source for scientists worldwide. A key focus for Kew Bulletin is to accelerate the pace of new species descriptions. In an era of unprec- edented biodiversity loss, documenting the planet S incredible plant and fungal diversity is more crucial than ever.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What primarily influences ecosystem functioning and the associated ecosystem services?
nodes.answer: Biodiversity primarily influences ecosystem functioning and the associated ecosystem services.
nodes.paragraph: These ecosystem services depend on the good functioning of ecosystems, which in turn is the result of the rich interactions between species, as well as between species and their environments. Simply said, ecosystem functioning and the resulting ecosystem services depend primarily on biodiversity (Hooper et al. 2005; Le Provost et al. 2023). The differ - ent health concepts EcoHealth, OneHealth, and Planetary Health (Lerner and Berg 2017), all suggest that biodiversity loss will lead to a degradation in ecosystem services which in turn will lead to increased health risks for humans, livestock, and wildlife (Schmeller et al. 2020). Pressures on ecosystems from stressors such as chemical pollution, habitat destruction, climate change, and introduced harmful species have constantly increased over the past decades. The series of Scientists Warnings all outline the consequences of those pres- sures on the global life-support system (Cavicchioli et al. 2019; Ripple et al. 2017; 2021; Schmeller et al. 2022). Some studies reported on the effects of water pollution on human health and well-being.

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Why has research on social and ecological systems been problematic according to the content?
nodes.answer: Research on social and ecological systems has been problematic because it has long been conducted independently without integrating them into coupled systems.
nodes.paragraph: Furthermore, compared to the SPEI threshold, the LUD threshold was stable at 0.24, demonstrating stronger robustness. This study provides a new perspective for understanding watershed SESs, and has important implications for sustainable ecosystem management and planning. Keywords Y angtze river basin, Socio-ecological systems, Land-use change, Climate change, Network analysis Since the onset of the Anthropocene, watershed environmental processes such as the hydrological cycle 1, water purification2,3, and flood regulation4 have been increasingly dominated by human activities and extreme climate events. The interactions between natural and human components within a watershed are characterized by complexity, nonlinearity, and uncertainty5,6. These complex dynamic interactions present challenges for decision- makers in formulating adaptive, integrated watershed management strategies, hindering the achievement of long-term sustainability goals 7,8. This requires recognizing the interdependence between society and nature through a socio-ecological system (SES) approach. SES is a coupled system of biophysical and human social elements that emphasizes the integrity and coordination between ecosystems and social systems9. However, research on social and ecological systems has long been conducted independently, without integrating them into coupled systems10.

nodes.answer: The main objective of the study is to present the development of a participatory and replicable MCA methodology for identifying and prioritizing Nature-Based Solutions/Biodiversity Ecosystem Services (NBS/BES) that cover the WEFE nexus and impact socio-economic parameters.
nodes.paragraph: Maleki et al. (2018) [ 28] apply Multicriteria-Spatial Decision Support System (MSDSS) for prioritization of wetland restoration using different scenarios. MCA has also been used for area prioritization through ranking of criteria. Valente et al. (2021) [29] used a mixed method of participatory analysis and multi-criteria evaluation to identify priority areas for forest restoration coupled with water related ecosystem services. The typical structure of MCA includes the identification of the relevant criteria and alter - natives from the existing theory and practice, the assignment of numerical values to criteria to indicate their relative importance and to quantify the impacts of the alternatives on these criteria, and the use of a formal mathematical procedure for analyzing numerical values to determine the ranking (priorities) of the alternatives [ 30]. The objective of this study is to present the development of a participatory and replicable MCA methodology and its application at in-person or online workshops, through a tool for identifying and prioritizing NBS/BES that cover the WEFE nexus and have a considerable impact on socio-economic parameters [ 2, 4].

nodes.question: What role do small terrestrial mammals play in ecosystems?
nodes.answer: Small terrestrial mammals are an integral part of biodiversity and serve as a major food source for birds of prey and small carnivores.
nodes.paragraph: 2015). While the conservation threats faced by large mammals are known to most people, as these are known as flagship species and are the focus of conservation strategies and campaigns by major conservation and environmental organizations (e.g., giant panda, whales, wolf, wildcat, European otter), threats to small mammals are often less well known (exempting perhaps bats or dormice) and therefore often go unnoticed. In addition, most small mammals are harder to observe or even to detect and their natural history is relatively unknown. Nevertheless, they are an integral part of biodiversity and play a key role in ecosystems, as they are an important part in food chains. nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are bryophytes, and why are they important in agricultural grasslands?
nodes.answer: Bryophytes are non-vascular plants that include mosses, liverworts, and hornworts, and they play a key role in biodiversity by forming a distinct layer on the soil surface and contributing to ecosystem functions like water regulation and nutrient cycling in agricultural grasslands.
nodes.paragraph: These changes in the vascular plant community might lead to small plants such as bryophytes being lost due to light competition 7. Bryophytes, comprising mosses, liverworts, and hornworts 8, can be an important part of the biodiversity of agricultural grasslands and can form a distinct layer on the soil surface below vascular plants 9. They further contribute to important ecosystem functions such as water and microclimate regulation and nutrient cycling 10 12. While changes in community composition following land-use intensification have been well studied for some taxa such as vascular plants, bryophytes have only rarely been considered. Understanding the mechanisms behind land-use effects on bryophytes is critical to promote restoration of bryophyte communities. Nitrogen could affect bryophytes directly, but also indirectly via changing vascular plant community composition. Nitrogen can harm bryophytes directly due to: ammonium toxicity 13,14, osmotic effects, which can lead to browning of the tissues 15, and physiological processes, such as a disturbance of their carbon metabolism 16. But bryophytes can also benefit from nitrogen to a certain degree: studies have found that bryophyte growth increases up to moderate levels of fertilization 17,18.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why is experimental study important in understanding the effect of vascular plant richness on bryophytes?
nodes.answer: Experimental studies are needed to test the effect of vascular plant richness on bryophytes as it has rarely been investigated through manipulative experiments.
nodes.paragraph: Experimental studies are needed to test this but the effect of vascular plant richness on bryophytes has only rarely been investigated in experiments manipulating vascular plant species number 31,32. Changes in the functional composition of vascular plants following nitrogen enrichment could also influence bryophytes. A key axis of vascular plant functional composition variation is the leaf economics spectrum 33,34, distinguishing fast from slow growth strategy, which can be represented by traits such as specific leaf area (SLA) 35. Fast-growing communities with a high mean SLA are adapted to nutrient-rich conditions and might therefore produce more biomass, which in turn reduces light availability. However, fast vascular plant communities also have more rapidly decomposing litter and thus less organic material buildup on the ground 36, which might benefit bryophytes. Slow vascular plant species are well adapted to drought 30 and could thus provide a moister microclimate in summer which might facilitate bryophyte survival during dry periods. Because bryophytes take up nutrients over the whole surface area of their leaves, they react quickly to changes in their environments 37 and could be influenced by the conditions that fast- or slow-growing vascular plant communities produce.
